![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/85f2356d-c30a-498a-8a2d-2d00e12cf3d4)

So this is my first foray into godot code, so I'm probably not the best person to be deciding how this should be solved... perhaps those who have commented are the greater experts on SDL joypad inputs and how this should jive with GODOT.

Having said that, I think GODOT may need a way to disambiguate HAT vs. Buttons in that mapping... and I say there is a way... if buttons you use 'b' in mapping file.  If axis you use 'a,' and hat you use 'h.'  This is currently done and yet hat events are being generated.  There is the error.  Code is not doing the will of the mapping file.  It is sending those double events.
  * I'm thinking only one event should be sent and somehow and should be button or hat depending on 'b' or 'h.'
  * Of course, if you map dpleft:b15 and dpleft:h0.8   --> then yes, send double events.  Not sure if SDL2 allows this.

However, it is interesting that sdl-jstest seems to have the same issue?  As it says one hat is detected?

Perhaps this should be addressed in: platform/linuxbsd/joypad_linux.cpp?
If anyone could be so kind to advise me the things I'm missing.

As above, I'm a confused about how hat events are being generated from SDL, but it is worth noting two things:
(1) I tried running this on windows, I got **similar** results.
In Linux when I have left and right pressed, I get "right."   In windows I get nothing.
In Linux when I have up and down pressed, I get "down"   In windows I get nothing.

I think windows is correct for that HAT implementation (IMHO).  If both inputs are down, there should be no output.
I think linux is closer to correct for button implementation - at least I get right or down in the case of two outputs.

(2) when running sdl-jstest

I suggest you use [`evemu-record`](https://www.freedesktop.org/wiki/Evemu/) to see the key events.

You can refer to the [Linux Gamepad Specification](https://docs.kernel.org/input/gamepad.html#linux-gamepad-specification). However, Godot does not use [`EV_SYN`](https://docs.kernel.org/input/event-codes.html#event-types) to separate events. So there is no way to combine multiple events into one input event. Moreover, `ABS_HAT0X`/`ABS_HAT0Y` are hardcoded to map to `DPAD`.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/0f20e67d8de83c30b5dd79cb68d12d4cf613065d/platform/linuxbsd/joypad_linux.cpp#L544-L574

This is not good for devices where trigger buttons can be available as both digital (`BTN_DPAD_*`) and analog (`ABS_HAT0X` and `ABS_HAT0Y`) buttons.

In this wiki, there are some notes on dance pads: https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Gamepad

> **_3.1_ Dance pads**
> Most dance pads should work. However some pads, especially those used from a video game console via an adapter, have a tendency to map the directional buttons as axis buttons. This prevents hitting left-right or up-down simultaneously. This behavior can be fixed for devices recognized by xpad via a module option: 

```
# modprobe -r xpad
# modprobe xpad dpad_to_buttons=1
```
> If that did not work, you can try [axisfix-git](https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/axisfix-git/)AUR or patching the joydev kernel module (https://github.com/adiel-mittmann/dancepad).

Yours doesn't seem to map to axis buttons, that's good.

And there's https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/v6.13/input/devices/xpad.html#xbox-dance-pads
> Known dance pads automatically map the d-pad to buttons and will work correctly out of the box.

Judging from the docs, I'd say the intended target are the joypad dpad buttons, and not X/Y/A/B.

As stated here: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/99513#issuecomment-2492916639, Godot releases the opposite dpad button, which prevents the dance pad from working.  
[Doubts about this have come up since.](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/42200#issuecomment-2714575049).  
And even though Godot tries to prevent it, it can still happen (depending on the joypad): https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/42200, but that is [because release and new button press can be out of order](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/42200#issuecomment-2714414966), _which is a different issue_.

**All things considered, the forced release should be removed.**

In the meantime, this issue's tags can be changed: remove "**needs testing**" (Godot code proves that the opposite dpad button is auto-cleared), and add "**discussion**"

It's [been said](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/106218#issuecomment-3008572985) that https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/106218 may have fixed this (even if @MJacred 's comment above hints this is intentional). Can this be verified?
